title: ExpTrialMng: A Universal Experiment Trial Manager for AR/VR/MR Experiments Based on Unity
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a practical software problem in VR/AR/MR research: many researchers want to run user experiments in immersive environments, but existing tools can be too complex, too heavy, or too tied to specific workflows. The authors argue that these barriers are especially problematic for researchers who are not proficient in Unity programming, and that unexpected hardware issues such as tracking loss can interrupt experiments and cause data loss.

To address this, they propose ExpTrialMng, a Unity library for managing experimental trials. The library reads pre-generated CSV trial files, delivers trial settings to an experiment manager, saves results to a CSV file after each trial, and supports restarting the experiment from a specific trial number after an interruption. The approach is meant to be lightweight and general-purpose so it can be adapted to many VR/AR HCI or psychology experiments without needing extensive custom code.

The paper is not an empirical study with human participants; instead, it is a framework paper describing the design and functionality of the library. The main conclusion is that ExpTrialMng can lower the programming barrier for immersive-experiment researchers, reduce data loss from technical problems, and make experiment implementation more universal across VR/AR settings.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a tooling/preprint paper describing a software library, not an empirical study of learning or user outcomes. It does not present a controlled evaluation with participant outcomes or effect estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational or achievement impact is measured. The contribution is infrastructural (experiment management) rather than an intervention with demonstrated outcome effects.

interventions.use_case: Unity-based trial management library for VR/AR/MR experiments that handles pre-generated trial sequencing, result saving, and resuming experiments after interruptions
